reviewAdvisory: The draft asserts a downward cost direction for extraction, but the supplied figures contain no cost, production, or market data from which that direction can be derived; it is an inference presented as a cost conclusion.

The table assigns 'downward pressure' on extraction and exploration costs across resource types, but no figure in the record supports a cost direction; the table converts a depth milestone into a cost judgement the evidence does not contain.

The figures state a previous international depth record of 1,419 meters and a new maximum of 2,004.8 meters, but do not establish that China 'holds the record'; the draft upgrades a single trial result into a standing record claim.

The confidence section labels the cost implications as inferred, while the body states them as directional conclusions ('point toward lower per-unit extraction costs', 'Downward pressure'), so the two sections disagree on how firm the cost claim is.
Every figure rests on one announcement carried by one outlet, and the body presents the record and capability claims without a plain single-source disclosure sentence outside the confidence section.

The ratio 2,004.8 / 1,419 is arithmetically correct, but the draft presents it as a capability multiple without noting that the two figures are a single trial depth and a prior record, not comparable operating baselines.
